Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Exercises ./ledger against a fresh database and compares every command's exit code and standard\n# output with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/LayersTesting/bin/run.sh APP  from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a\n# SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory. Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/seed_accounts.csv\" ]; then SEED=$HERE; else SEED=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nLEDGER=\"$APP/ledger\"\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nDATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-$WORK/ledger.db}\nexport DATABASE_URL\n\nif [ ! -x \"$LEDGER\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./ledger at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <ledger args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$LEDGER\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: ledger $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: ledger $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L124iSpbUb6cLjeBLgHjLp","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"``ledger load`` commands: ``accounts`` and ``categories`` are all-or-nothing bulk loads.\n\nEvery row of the file is checked before the first write: the key, the text, the key's repetition\nwithin the file, and the key's presence in the store. The rows are then inserted through\n``ledger_core.atomic.run_all``, so a failing insert removes the rows already stored.\n\n``transactions`` is still a placeholder: it reads and header-checks the file, then exits 1 because\nnothing is loaded, rather than reporting a load that did not happen.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\n\nfrom cli.registry import Command\nfrom ledger_core.atomic import run_all\nfrom ledger_core.csvio import read_rows\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational, Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.validation import validate_code, validate_name\n\nACCOUNT_HEADER = (\"account\", \"name\")\nCATEGORY_HEADER = (\"category\", \"description\")\nTRANSACTION_HEADER = (\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\")\n\n\ndef _checked_rows(\n    path: str,\n    header: tuple[str, str],\n    validate_key: Callable[[str], str],\n    stored: Iterable[str],\n) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate every row of ``path`` before any write; return ``(key, text)`` pairs in file order.\"\"\"\n    already_stored = set(stored)\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    checked: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    for line, (key_text, text) in read_rows(path, header):\n        try:\n            key = validate_key(key_text)\n            validate_name(text)\n        except Rejected as exc:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: {exc}\") from exc\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} repeats within the file\")\n        if key in already_stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n        checked.append((key, text))\n    return checked\n\n\ndef _load(\n    path: str,\n    header: tuple[str, str],\n    table: str,\n    validate_key: Callable[[str], str],\n    stored: Iterable[str],\n    create: Callable[[str, str], object],\n    remove: Callable[[str], object],\n) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Check the whole file, insert every row as one unit, and report the loaded count.\"\"\"\n    checked = _checked_rows(path, header, validate_key, stored)\n    run_all([(_insert(create, key, text), _remove(remove, key)) for key, text in checked])\n    return [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [table, str(len(checked))]]\n\n\ndef _insert(create: Callable[[str, str], object], key: str, text: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: create(key, text)\n\n\ndef _remove(remove: Callable[[str], object], key: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: remove(key)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``account,name`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        ACCOUNT_HEADER,\n        \"accounts\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.account for row in db.accounts.list()),\n        lambda key, name: db.accounts.create(account=key, name=name),\n        lambda key: db.accounts.delete(account=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef load_categories(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``category,description`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        CATEGORY_HEADER,\n        \"categories\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.category for row in db.categories.list()),\n        lambda key, text: db.categories.create(category=key, description=text),\n        lambda key: db.categories.delete(category=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef _transactions_placeholder(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    read_rows(args[0], TRANSACTION_HEADER)\n    raise Operational(\"loading transactions is not implemented yet\")\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"load\", \"accounts\"): Command(load_accounts, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"categories\"): Command(load_categories, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"transactions\"): Command(_transactions_placeholder, 1, 1),\n}\n---REG\n\"\"\"Command registry: maps command words to handlers, filled from the modules in ``cli/commands/``.\"\"\"\n\nimport importlib\nimport pkgutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom typing import Any, NamedTuple\n\nfrom cli import commands\n\n\nclass Command(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"One registered command. ``max_args`` is ``None`` when the argument count is unbounded.\"\"\"\n\n    handler: Callable[[Any, list[str]], list[list[str]]]\n    min_args: int\n    max_args: int | None\n\n\n#: Command words, such as ``(\"account\", \"add\")``, mapped to their command.\nCOMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], Command] = {}\n\n\ndef load() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Import every module in ``cli/commands/`` and add its ``COMMANDS``. Idempotent; never removes.\"\"\"\n    for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(commands.__path__):\n        module = importlib.import_module(f\"{commands.__name__}.{module_info.name}\")\n        COMMANDS.update(getattr(module, \"COMMANDS\", {}))\n---INIT\n\"\"\"Command-line entry point for the ledger.\n\n``main`` resolves the command words, checks the argument count, opens the database, calls the\nhandler, and turns the result into CSV on stdout or one diagnostic line on stderr. It returns the\nexit code and never calls ``sys.exit``; the ``ledger`` launcher is the only caller that does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError, Operational\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_OPERATIONAL = 1\nEXIT_USAGE = 2\nPOSTGRES_PREFIXES = (\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")\n\n\ndef _usage_error(message: str) -> int:\n    print(f\"usage: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return EXIT_USAGE\n\n\ndef _open_store(location: str) -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the declared store. A SQLite file whose directory is absent is refused, not created.\n\n    The shipped SQLite driver creates a missing parent directory on connect, which would turn a\n    mistyped location into a new, empty store. The ledger's store is provisioned in advance.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not location.startswith(POSTGRES_PREFIXES):\n        parent = Path(location).parent\n        if not parent.is_dir():\n            raise Operational(f\"database directory does not exist: {parent}\")\n    return open_database(location)\n\n\ndef _match(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], registry.Command] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the longest command-word prefix of ``argv`` that is registered, with its command.\"\"\"\n    for length in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        words = tuple(argv[:length])\n        if words in registry.COMMANDS:\n            return words, registry.COMMANDS[words]\n    return None\n\n\ndef _format(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as unquoted CSV with ``\\\\n`` line endings.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(\",\".join(str(value) for value in row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)\n    registry.load()\n\n    matched = _match(argv)\n    if matched is None:\n        return _usage_error(f\"unknown command {' '.join(argv)!r}\" if argv else \"no command given\")\n    words, command = matched\n\n    args = argv[len(words):]\n    if len(args) < command.min_args or (command.max_args is not None and len(args) > command.max_args):\n        return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {' '.join(words)!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        database = _open_store(database_path())\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: cannot open database: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n\n    try:\n        rows = command.handler(database, args)\n    except LedgerError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n    sys.stdout.write(_format(rows))\n    return EXIT_OK\n---CSV\n\"\"\"Shared CSV reader for the ``ledger load`` commands.\n\nThe reader only reads: it never touches the database and never writes to a file.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational, Rejected\n\nRow = tuple[int, list[str]]\n\n\ndef read_rows(path: str, header: Sequence[str]) -> list[Row]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(line_number, fields)`` for every data row of ``path``, in file order.\n\n    ``header`` lists the column names the table requires, in order. Line numbers are 1-based, so the\n    first data row after a header on line 1 is line 2. Blank lines are skipped. Raises ``Operational``\n    when the file cannot be read or decoded, and ``Rejected`` when the header differs, the file is\n    empty, or a data row's field count differs from ``len(header)``.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            return _read(fh, path, list(header))\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise Operational(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}\") from exc\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise Operational(f\"cannot decode {path} as UTF-8: {exc}\") from exc\n\n\ndef _read(fh, path: str, header: list[str]) -> list[Row]:\n    reader = csv.reader(fh)\n    try:\n        first = next(reader, None)\n        if first is None:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} is empty; expected header {','.join(header)}\")\n        if first != header:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line 1: header must be {','.join(header)}\")\n        rows: list[Row] = []\n        for fields in reader:\n            if not fields:\n                continue\n            if len(fields) != len(header):\n                raise Rejected(\n                    f\"{path} line {reader.line_num}: expected {len(header)} fields, found {len(fields)}\"\n                )\n            rows.append((reader.line_num, fields))\n        return rows\n    except csv.Error as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {reader.line_num}: malformed CSV: {exc}\") from exc\n---VAL\n\"\"\"Pure validation of codes, names, memos, and dates.\n\nEach function returns the validated value unchanged, or raises ``Rejected``. Nothing here touches\nstorage or prints anything.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nimport re\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\n\nCODE_MAX = 12\nNAME_MAX = 40\nMEMO_MAX = 60\n\n_CODE = re.compile(r\"[A-Z0-9]{1,%d}\" % CODE_MAX)\n_DATE = re.compile(r\"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})\")\n_FORBIDDEN_TEXT = (\",\", \"\\n\", \"\\r\")\n\n\ndef _require_text(value: object, label: str) -> str:\n    if not isinstance(value, str):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be text\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _check_length(value: str, label: str, low: int, high: int) -> None:\n    if not low <= len(value) <= high:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be {low} to {high} characters\")\n\n\ndef _check_plain_text(value: str, label: str) -> None:\n    if any(mark in value for mark in _FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must not contain a comma or newline\")\n\n\ndef validate_code(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 1 to 12 characters, each ``A-Z`` or ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"code\")\n    if not _CODE.fullmatch(text):\n        raise Rejected(\"code must be 1 to 12 characters from A-Z and 0-9\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_name(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 1 to 40 characters with no comma or newline.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"name\")\n    _check_length(text, \"name\", 1, NAME_MAX)\n    _check_plain_text(text, \"name\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_memo(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 0 to 60 characters with no comma or newline.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"memo\")\n    _check_length(text, \"memo\", 0, MEMO_MAX)\n    _check_plain_text(text, \"memo\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_date(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept a real calendar date written ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"date\")\n    match = _DATE.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(\"date must be written YYYY-MM-DD\")\n    year, month, day = (int(part) for part in match.groups())\n    try:\n        datetime.date(year, month, day)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"date is not a real calendar date: {text}\") from exc\n    return value\n---BAL\n\"\"\"Balance rule: a proposed set of transaction changes must leave no account below zero.\n\nAn account's balance is the sum of its stored transaction amounts in integer cents. The check only\nreads through the persistence interface and never writes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Union\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import NotFound, Rejected\nfrom persistence import Database\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Insert:\n    \"\"\"A transaction to be added to ``account`` with ``amount`` cents.\"\"\"\n\n    account: str\n    amount: int\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Edit:\n    \"\"\"A stored transaction whose amount becomes ``amount`` cents.\"\"\"\n\n    txn_id: int\n    amount: int\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Delete:\n    \"\"\"A stored transaction to be removed.\"\"\"\n\n    txn_id: int\n\n\nChange = Union[Insert, Edit, Delete]\n\n\ndef current_balance(db: Database, account: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the sum of the stored amounts of ``account``; ``0`` when it has none.\"\"\"\n    return sum(row.amount for row in db.transactions.list(account=account))\n\n\ndef _stored(db: Database, txn_id: int):\n    stored = db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id)\n    if stored is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    return stored\n\n\ndef _net_deltas(db: Database, changes: list[Change]) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Group the changes by account and sum each account's net effect in cents.\"\"\"\n    deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for change in changes:\n        if isinstance(change, Insert):\n            account, delta = change.account, change.amount\n        elif isinstance(change, Edit):\n            stored = _stored(db, change.txn_id)\n            account, delta = stored.account, change.amount - stored.amount\n        elif isinstance(change, Delete):\n            stored = _stored(db, change.txn_id)\n            account, delta = stored.account, -stored.amount\n        else:\n            raise Rejected(f\"unknown transaction change: {change!r}\")\n        deltas[account] = deltas.get(account, 0) + delta\n    return deltas\n\n\ndef check_no_negative(db: Database, changes: list[Change]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise ``Rejected`` when any affected account's resulting balance is below zero.\n\n    Changes are judged together by their net effect per account, so their order does not matter.\n    A resulting balance of exactly zero is allowed. Accounts the changes do not touch are not judged.\n    \"\"\"\n    for account, delta in _net_deltas(db, list(changes)).items():\n        resulting = current_balance(db, account) + delta\n        if resulting < 0:\n            raise Rejected(f\"account {account} would be overdrawn by {-resulting} cents\")\n---TXN\n\"\"\"Transaction rows: formatting a stored transaction for output, the next free id, and id parsing.\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Union\n\nfrom persistence import Database\nfrom persistence.schema import (\n    TransactionsCreateOutput,\n    TransactionsGetOutput,\n    TransactionsListOutput,\n    TransactionsUpdateOutput,\n)\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.money import format_cents\n\nStoredTxn = Union[TransactionsCreateOutput, TransactionsGetOutput, TransactionsListOutput, TransactionsUpdateOutput]\n\n_TXN_ID = re.compile(r\"-?[0-9]+\")\n\n\ndef parse_txn_id(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Parse a transaction id written as an integer. Any other text is rejected.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(text, str) or _TXN_ID.fullmatch(text) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"transaction id must be an integer: {text!r}\")\n    return int(text)\n\n\ndef txn_row(txn: StoredTxn) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Format a stored transaction as the output row ``txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo``.\"\"\"\n    return [str(txn.txn_id), txn.date, txn.account, txn.category, format_cents(txn.amount), txn.memo]\n\n\ndef next_txn_id(db: Database) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the largest stored ``txn_id`` plus one, or ``1`` when the ledger has no transactions.\"\"\"\n    return max((txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()), default=0) + 1\n---MONEY\n\"\"\"Conversion between amount text and integer cents.\n\nAmounts are signed integer cents everywhere. Parsing and formatting use integer arithmetic only.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\n\n_AMOUNT = re.compile(r\"(-?)([0-9]+)(?:\\.([0-9]{1,2}))?\")\n\n\ndef parse_amount(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Parse ``-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`` into integer cents. Zero and three or more decimals are rejected.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(text, str):\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must be text\")\n    match = _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"amount must look like -12.50 with at most two decimals: {text!r}\")\n    sign, whole, fraction = match.groups()\n    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or \"\").ljust(2, \"0\"))\n    if cents == 0:\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must not be zero\")\n    return -cents if sign else cents\n\n\ndef format_cents(cents: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render integer cents with exactly two decimals, a leading ``-`` when negative, no separators.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(cents, int) or isinstance(cents, bool):\n        raise Rejected(\"cents must be an integer\")\n    sign = \"-\" if cents < 0 else \"\"\n    magnitude = abs(cents)\n    return f\"{sign}{magnitude // 100}.{magnitude % 100:02d}\"\n---ERR\n\"\"\"Domain errors. Each carries the process exit code the CLI reports.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LedgerError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for every domain error the ledger raises.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code: int\n\n\nclass Rejected(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or negative balance.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 3\n\n\nclass NotFound(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An account or transaction is absent on get, rename, delete, or amend.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 4\n\n\nclass Operational(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An unreadable file or an unopenable database.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 1","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3d6c23d9-bd7a-4743-8d5d-6d8e6078828d","uuid":"2140abe9-dca7-47dc-ab9f-7e46c75ff1ec","timestamp":"2026-10-27T14:53:11.284Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"``ledger load`` commands: ``accounts`` and ``categories`` are all-or-nothing bulk loads.\n\nEvery row of the file is checked before the first write: the key, the text, the key's repetition\nwithin the file, and the key's presence in the store. return ``(key, text)`` pairs in file order.\"\"\"\n    already_stored = set(stored)\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    checked: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    for line, (key_text, text) in read_rows(path, header):\n        try:\n            key = validate_key(key_text)\n            validate_name(text)\n        except Rejected as exc:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: {exc}\") from exc\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} repeats within the file\")\n        if key in already_stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n        checked.append((key, text))\n    return checked\n\n\ndef _load(\n    path: str,\n    header: tuple[str, str],\n    table: str,\n    validate_key: Callable[[str], str],\n    stored: Iterable[str],\n    create: Callable[[str, str], object],\n    remove: Callable[[str], object],\n) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Check the whole file, insert every row as one unit, and report the loaded count.\"\"\"\n    checked = _checked_rows(path, header, validate_key, stored)\n    run_all([(_insert(create, key, text), _remove(remove, key)) for key, text in checked])\n    return [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [table, str(len(checked))]]\n\n\ndef _insert(create: Callable[[str, str], object], key: str, text: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: create(key, text)\n\n\ndef _remove(remove: Callable[[str], object], key: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: remove(key)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``account,name`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        ACCOUNT_HEADER,\n        \"accounts\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.account for row in db.accounts.list()),\n        lambda key, name: db.accounts.create(account=key, name=name),\n        lambda key: db.accounts.delete(account=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef load_categories(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``category,description`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        CATEGORY_HEADER,\n        \"categories\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.category for row in db.categories.list()),\n        lambda key, text: db.categories.create(category=key, description=text),\n        lambda key: db.categories.delete(category=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef _transactions_placeholder(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    read_rows(args[0], TRANSACTION_HEADER)\n    raise Operational(\"loading transactions is not implemented yet\")\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"load\", \"accounts\"): Command(load_accounts, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"categories\"): Command(load_categories, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"transactions\"): Command(_transactions_placeholder, 1, 1),\n}\n---REG\n\"\"\"Command registry: maps command words to handlers, filled from the modules in ``cli/commands/``.\"\"\"\n\nimport importlib\nimport pkgutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom typing import Any, NamedTuple\n\nfrom cli import commands\n\n\nclass Command(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"One registered command. ``max_args`` is ``None`` when the argument count is unbounded.\"\"\"\n\n    handler: Callable[[Any, list[str]], list[list[str]]]\n    min_args: int\n    max_args: int | None\n\n\n#: Command words, such as ``(\"account\", \"add\")``, mapped to their command.\nCOMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], Command] = {}\n\n\ndef load() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Import every module in ``cli/commands/`` and add its ``COMMANDS``. Idempotent; never removes.\"\"\"\n    for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(commands.__path__):\n        module = importlib.import_module(f\"{commands.__name__}.{module_info.name}\")\n        COMMANDS.update(getattr(module, \"COMMANDS\", {}))\n---INIT\n\"\"\"Command-line entry point for the ledger.\n\n``main`` resolves the command words, checks the argument count, opens the database, calls the\nhandler, and turns the result into CSV on stdout or one diagnostic line on stderr. It returns the\nexit code and never calls ``sys.exit``; the ``ledger`` launcher is the only caller that does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError, Operational\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_OPERATIONAL = 1\nEXIT_USAGE = 2\nPOSTGRES_PREFIXES = (\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")\n\n\ndef _usage_error(message: str) -> int:\n    print(f\"usage: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return EXIT_USAGE\n\n\ndef _open_store(location: str) -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the declared store. A SQLite file whose directory is absent is refused, not created.\n\n    The shipped SQLite driver creates a missing parent directory on connect, which would turn a\n    mistyped location into a new, empty store. The ledger's store is provisioned in advance.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not location.startswith(POSTGRES_PREFIXES):\n        parent = Path(location).parent\n        if not parent.is_dir():\n            raise Operational(f\"database directory does not exist: {parent}\")\n    return open_database(location)\n\n\ndef _match(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], registry.Command] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the longest command-word prefix of ``argv`` that is registered, with its command.\"\"\"\n    for length in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        words = tuple(argv[:length])\n        if words in registry.COMMANDS:\n            return words, registry.COMMANDS[words]\n    return None\n\n\ndef _format(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as unquoted CSV with ``\\\\n`` line endings.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(\",\".join(str(value) for value in row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)\n    registry.load()\n\n    matched = _match(argv)\n    if matched is None:\n        return _usage_error(f\"unknown command {' '.join(argv)!r}\" if argv else \"no command given\")\n    words, command = matched\n\n    args = argv[len(words):]\n    if len(args) < command.min_args or (command.max_args is not None and len(args) > command.max_args):\n        return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {' '.join(words)!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        database = _open_store(database_path())\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: cannot open database: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n\n    try:\n        rows = command.handler(database, args)\n    except LedgerError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n    sys.stdout.write(_format(rows))\n    return EXIT_OK\n---CSV\n\"\"\"Shared CSV reader for the ``ledger load`` commands.\n\nThe reader only reads: it never touches the database and never writes to a file.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational, Rejected\n\nRow = tuple[int, list[str]]\n\n\ndef read_rows(path: str, header: Sequence[str]) -> list[Row]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(line_number, fields)`` for every data row of ``path``, in file order.\n\n    ``header`` lists the column names the table requires, in order. Line numbers are 1-based, so the\n    first data row after a header on line 1 is line 2. Blank lines are skipped. Raises ``Operational``\n    when the file cannot be read or decoded, and ``Rejected`` when the header differs, the file is\n    empty, or a data row's field count differs from ``len(header)``.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            return _read(fh, path, list(header))\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise Operational(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}\") from exc\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise Operational(f\"cannot decode {path} as UTF-8: {exc}\") from exc\n\n\ndef _read(fh, path: str, header: list[str]) -> list[Row]:\n    reader = csv.reader(fh)\n    try:\n        first = next(reader, None)\n        if first is None:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} is empty; expected header {','.join(header)}\")\n        if first != header:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line 1: header must be {','.join(header)}\")\n        rows: list[Row] = []\n        for fields in reader:\n            if not fields:\n                continue\n            if len(fields) != len(header):\n                raise Rejected(\n                    f\"{path} line {reader.line_num}: expected {len(header)} fields, found {len(fields)}\"\n                )\n            rows.append((reader.line_num, fields))\n        return rows\n    except csv.Error as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {reader.line_num}: malformed CSV: {exc}\") from exc\n---VAL\n\"\"\"Pure validation of codes, names, memos, and dates.\n\nEach function returns the validated value unchanged, or raises ``Rejected``. Nothing here touches\nstorage or prints anything.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nimport re\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\n\nCODE_MAX = 12\nNAME_MAX = 40\nMEMO_MAX = 60\n\n_CODE = re.compile(r\"[A-Z0-9]{1,%d}\" % CODE_MAX)\n_DATE = re.compile(r\"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})\")\n_FORBIDDEN_TEXT = (\",\", \"\\n\", \"\\r\")\n\n\ndef _require_text(value: object, label: str) -> str:\n    if not isinstance(value, str):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be text\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _check_length(value: str, label: str, low: int, high: int) -> None:\n    if not low <= len(value) <= high:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be {low} to {high} characters\")\n\n\ndef _check_plain_text(value: str, label: str) -> None:\n    if any(mark in value for mark in _FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must not contain a comma or newline\")\n\n\ndef validate_code(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 1 to 12 characters, each ``A-Z`` or ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"code\")\n    if not _CODE.fullmatch(text):\n        raise Rejected(\"code must be 1 to 12 characters from A-Z and 0-9\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_name(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 1 to 40 characters with no comma or newline.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"name\")\n    _check_length(text, \"name\", 1, NAME_MAX)\n    _check_plain_text(text, \"name\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_memo(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept 0 to 60 characters with no comma or newline.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"memo\")\n    _check_length(text, \"memo\", 0, MEMO_MAX)\n    _check_plain_text(text, \"memo\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef validate_date(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Accept a real calendar date written ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    text = _require_text(value, \"date\")\n    match = _DATE.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(\"date must be written YYYY-MM-DD\")\n    year, month, day = (int(part) for part in match.groups())\n    try:\n        datetime.date(year, month, day)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"date is not a real calendar date: {text}\") from exc\n    return value\n---BAL\n\"\"\"Balance rule: a proposed set of transaction changes must leave no account below zero.\n\nAn account's balance is the sum of its stored transaction amounts in integer cents. The check only\nreads through the persistence interface and never writes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Union\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import NotFound, Rejected\nfrom persistence import Database\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Insert:\n    \"\"\"A transaction to be added to ``account`` with ``amount`` cents.\"\"\"\n\n    account: str\n    amount: int\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Edit:\n    \"\"\"A stored transaction whose amount becomes ``amount`` cents.\"\"\"\n\n    txn_id: int\n    amount: int\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Delete:\n    \"\"\"A stored transaction to be removed.\"\"\"\n\n    txn_id: int\n\n\nChange = Union[Insert, Edit, Delete]\n\n\ndef current_balance(db: Database, account: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the sum of the stored amounts of ``account``; ``0`` when it has none.\"\"\"\n    return sum(row.amount for row in db.transactions.list(account=account))\n\n\ndef _stored(db: Database, txn_id: int):\n    stored = db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id)\n    if stored is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    return stored\n\n\ndef _net_deltas(db: Database, changes: list[Change]) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Group the changes by account and sum each account's net effect in cents.\"\"\"\n    deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for change in changes:\n        if isinstance(change, Insert):\n            account, delta = change.account, change.amount\n        elif isinstance(change, Edit):\n            stored = _stored(db, change.txn_id)\n            account, delta = stored.account, change.amount - stored.amount\n        elif isinstance(change, Delete):\n            stored = _stored(db, change.txn_id)\n            account, delta = stored.account, -stored.amount\n        else:\n            raise Rejected(f\"unknown transaction change: {change!r}\")\n        deltas[account] = deltas.get(account, 0) + delta\n    return deltas\n\n\ndef check_no_negative(db: Database, changes: list[Change]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise ``Rejected`` when any affected account's resulting balance is below zero.\n\n    Changes are judged together by their net effect per account, so their order does not matter.\n    A resulting balance of exactly zero is allowed. Accounts the changes do not touch are not judged.\n    \"\"\"\n    for account, delta in _net_deltas(db, list(changes)).items():\n        resulting = current_balance(db, account) + delta\n        if resulting < 0:\n            raise Rejected(f\"account {account} would be overdrawn by {-resulting} cents\")\n---TXN\n\"\"\"Transaction rows: formatting a stored transaction for output, the next free id, and id parsing.\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Union\n\nfrom persistence import Database\nfrom persistence.schema import (\n    TransactionsCreateOutput,\n    TransactionsGetOutput,\n    TransactionsListOutput,\n    TransactionsUpdateOutput,\n)\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.money import format_cents\n\nStoredTxn = Union[TransactionsCreateOutput, TransactionsGetOutput, TransactionsListOutput, TransactionsUpdateOutput]\n\n_TXN_ID = re.compile(r\"-?[0-9]+\")\n\n\ndef parse_txn_id(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Parse a transaction id written as an integer. Any other text is rejected.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(text, str) or _TXN_ID.fullmatch(text) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"transaction id must be an integer: {text!r}\")\n    return int(text)\n\n\ndef txn_row(txn: StoredTxn) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Format a stored transaction as the output row ``txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo``.\"\"\"\n    return [str(txn.txn_id), txn.date, txn.account, txn.category, format_cents(txn.amount), txn.memo]\n\n\ndef next_txn_id(db: Database) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the largest stored ``txn_id`` plus one, or ``1`` when the ledger has no transactions.\"\"\"\n    return max((txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()), default=0) + 1\n---MONEY\n\"\"\"Conversion between amount text and integer cents.\n\nAmounts are signed integer cents everywhere. Parsing and formatting use integer arithmetic only.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Rejected\n\n_AMOUNT = re.compile(r\"(-?)([0-9]+)(?:\\.([0-9]{1,2}))?\")\n\n\ndef parse_amount(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Parse ``-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`` into integer cents. Zero and three or more decimals are rejected.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(text, str):\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must be text\")\n    match = _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"amount must look like -12.50 with at most two decimals: {text!r}\")\n    sign, whole, fraction = match.groups()\n    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or \"\").ljust(2, \"0\"))\n    if cents == 0:\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must not be zero\")\n    return -cents if sign else cents\n\n\ndef format_cents(cents: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render integer cents with exactly two decimals, a leading ``-`` when negative, no separators.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(cents, int) or isinstance(cents, bool):\n        raise Rejected(\"cents must be an integer\")\n    sign = \"-\" if cents < 0 else \"\"\n    magnitude = abs(cents)\n    return f\"{sign}{magnitude // 100}.{magnitude % 100:02d}\"\n---ERR\n\"\"\"Domain errors. Each carries the process exit code the CLI reports.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LedgerError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for every domain error the ledger raises.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code: int\n\n\nclass Rejected(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or negative balance.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 3\n\n\nclass NotFound(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An account or transaction is absent on get, rename, delete, or amend.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 4\n\n\nclass Operational(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An unreadable file or an unopenable database.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 1","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01L124iSpbUb6cLjeBLgHjLp","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PgHgetWZGEbTXCUQPGfDrx","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"All-or-nothing writes for commands that store more than one row.\n\nThe persistence layer commits each declared operation on its own, so this module cannot open one\ndatabase transaction around several writes. Callers therefore run every check before the first\nwrite. Each step then inserts one row; when a later insert fails, the rows already inserted are\ndeleted again, newest first, and the failure is reported as ``Operational``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational\nfrom persistence import PersistenceError\n\nStep = tuple[Callable[[], object], Callable[[], object]]\n\n\ndef run_all(steps: Sequence[Step]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run each ``(insert, undo)`` pair in order. On failure, undo the completed inserts and raise.\"\"\"\n    completed: list[Callable[[], object]] = []\n    for insert, undo in steps:\n        try:\n            insert()\n        except PersistenceError as exc:\n            for undo_done in reversed(completed):\n                undo_done()\n            raise Operational(f\"write failed and was rolled back: {exc}\") from exc\n        completed.append(undo)\n---ACC\n\"\"\"Account rows: the stored account and the live figures the account commands report.\n\n``account_row`` computes the transaction count and the integer-cent balance from the database on\nevery call, so neither figure is stored or embedded.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nAccountRow = tuple[str, str, int, int]\n\n\ndef account_row(db: Database, code: str) -> AccountRow | None:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(account, name, transactions, balance_cents)``, or ``None`` when the account is absent.\"\"\"\n    account = db.accounts.get(account=code)\n    if account is None:\n        return None\n    posted = db.transactions.list(account=code)\n    return (account.account, account.name, len(posted), sum(txn.amount for txn in posted))\n---CFG\n\"\"\"Runtime configuration: where the ledger database lives.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_URL_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef _non_empty(name: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the environment variable's value, or None when unset or empty.\"\"\"\n    value = os.environ.get(name)\n    return value if value else None\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Resolve the database location.\n\n    Precedence: ``DATABASE_URL`` (with an optional leading ``sqlite://`` removed),\n    then ``DATABASE_PATH``, then ``data/app.db``. Unset or empty values are skipped.\n    \"\"\"\n    url = _non_empty(\"DATABASE_URL\")\n    if url is not None:\n        return url.removeprefix(SQLITE_URL_PREFIX)\n    path = _non_empty(\"DATABASE_PATH\")\n    if path is not None:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n---TXNCMD\n\"\"\"Transaction commands: ``ledger txn post|get|delete|amend``.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.registry import Command\nfrom ledger_core.balances import Delete, Edit, Insert, check_no_negative\nfrom ledger_core.errors import NotFound, Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.money import parse_amount\nfrom ledger_core.transactions import next_txn_id, parse_txn_id, txn_row\nfrom ledger_core.validation import validate_date, validate_memo\n\nTXN_HEADER = [\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\"]\nDELETED_HEADER = [\"deleted\"]\n\n\ndef txn_post(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Check every input and the balance rule, then insert one transaction and print its row.\n\n    All checks run before the insert, so a rejected post stores nothing.\n    \"\"\"\n    account, category = args[0], args[1]\n    cents = parse_amount(args[2])\n    day = validate_date(args[3])\n    memo = validate_memo(args[4] if len(args) == 5 else \"\")\n    if db.accounts.get(account=account) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"account {account} does not exist\")\n    if db.categories.get(category=category) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"category {category} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Insert(account=account, amount=cents)])\n    txn = db.transactions.create(\n        txn_id=next_txn_id(db), date=day, account=account, category=category, amount=cents, memo=memo\n    )\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\ndef txn_get(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Print one stored transaction. Read-only; a non-integer id exits 3 and an absent id exits 4.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    txn = db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id)\n    if txn is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\ndef txn_delete(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Remove a transaction unless its account balance would go below zero without it.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    if db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id) is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Delete(txn_id=txn_id)])\n    db.transactions.delete(txn_id=txn_id)\n    return [DELETED_HEADER, [str(txn_id)]]\n\n\ndef txn_amend(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Change only the amount of a transaction, and only when its account stays at or above zero.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    cents = parse_amount(args[1])\n    if db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id) is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Edit(txn_id=txn_id, amount=cents)])\n    txn = db.transactions.update(txn_id=txn_id, amount=cents)\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"txn\", \"post\"): Command(txn_post, 4, 5),\n    (\"txn\", \"get\"): Command(txn_get, 1, 1),\n    (\"txn\", \"delete\"): Command(txn_delete, 1, 1),\n    (\"txn\", \"amend\"): Command(txn_amend, 2, 2),\n}\n---LEDGER\n#!/bin/sh\n# ledger: command-line cash ledger. Activates .venv when present and hands off to cli.main.\nset -eu\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$ROOT\"\nif [ -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1091\n    set +u; . .venv/bin/activate; set -u\nfi\nexec python -c 'import sys; from cli import main; sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))' \"$@\"\n---BIN\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Run Test Suite\n# Type: batch\n\n# --- Standard Preamble (POSIX sh) ---\nset -eu\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"\nLOG_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/data/logs\"\nmkdir -p \"$LOG_DIR\"\n\nTIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S')\nLOG_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/test_${TIMESTAMP}.log\"\nSTATUS_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/test_${TIMESTAMP}.status\"\n\necho \"=== test started at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ===\" | tee \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Arguments: $*\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Working dir: $PROJECT_DIR\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"---\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\n# Create the environment from the committed lock when it is missing.\nif [ ! -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then\n    uv sync --locked 2>&1 | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nfi\n\n# The pytest exit status is the verdict; tee would hide it, so record it to a file.\n# shellcheck disable=SC1091\n( set +u; . .venv/bin/activate; set -u; pytest -q \"$@\"; echo $? > \"$STATUS_FILE\" ) 2>&1 | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nstatus=$(cat \"$STATUS_FILE\")\nrm -f \"$STATUS_FILE\"\n\necho \"=== test finished at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') with exit $status ===\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nexit \"$status\"\n---PYPROJ\n[project]\nname = \"layerstesting\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = []\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n---CONF\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the ledger test suite.\n\nThe ``db_session`` and ``cli_runner`` fixtures delegate to helpers owned by the\ngenerated ``persistence`` package and the ``cli`` package. Those packages arrive\nwith their own stories, so the imports stay inside the fixtures until then.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Provisioned application store, supplied by ``persistence.testing``.\"\"\"\n    from persistence.testing import db_session as provision\n\n    return provision()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef cli_runner():\n    \"\"\"Command runner that invokes the ``ledger`` CLI, supplied by ``cli.testing``.\"\"\"\n    from cli.testing import cli_runner as provision\n\n    return provision()\n\"\"\"Fixtures shared by the command tests: a fresh, initialised ledger store per test under ``tmp_path``.\n\nCLI writes commit to their own connection, so these tests point ``DATABASE_URL`` at a private file.\nThat keeps ``data/app.db`` out of reach of anything a command does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom persistence import open_database\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef ledger_store(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Point the ledger at an empty, initialised store and return its path.\"\"\"\n    path = tmp_path / \"ledger.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", str(path))\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n    code, _, err = cli_runner(\"init\")\n    assert code == 0, err\n    return path\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef store_open():\n    \"\"\"Open the store at a path for read-back through the persistence interface.\"\"\"\n\n    def opener(path):\n        return open_database(str(path))\n\n    return opener\n---SCHEMA\n-- Generated by Drydock from DATABASE.md. Edit the declaration, not this file.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"accounts\" (\"account\" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, \"name\" TEXT NOT NULL);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"categories\" (\"category\" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, \"description\" TEXT NOT NULL);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions\" (\"txn_id\" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, \"date\" TEXT NOT NULL, \"account\" TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES \"accounts\"(\"account\"), \"category\" TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES \"categories\"(\"category\"), \"amount\" INTEGER NOT NULL, \"memo\" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '');\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_date_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\", \"date\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_category_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"category\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_category_date_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\", \"category\", \"date\");\n---GIT\n# Runtime\ndata/\n*.db\n*.log\n\n# Environment\n.env\n.venv/\nvenv/\n\n# Python\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n*.egg-info/\ndist/\nbuild/\n.pytest_cache/\n\n# OS\n.DS_Store\nThumbs.db","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3d6c23d9-bd7a-4743-8d5d-6d8e6078828d","uuid":"2f6701b1-de0f-47b2-be5f-51cfa3d9866c","timestamp":"2026-10-27T14:53:12.128Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"All-or-nothing writes for commands that store more than one row.\n\nThe persistence layer commits each declared operation on its own, so this module cannot open one\ndatabase transaction around several writes. Each step then inserts one row; when a later insert fails, the rows already inserted are\ndeleted again, newest first, and the failure is reported as ``Operational``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational\nfrom persistence import PersistenceError\n\nStep = tuple[Callable[[], object], Callable[[], object]]\n\n\ndef run_all(steps: Sequence[Step]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run each ``(insert, undo)`` pair in order. On failure, undo the completed inserts and raise.\"\"\"\n    completed: list[Callable[[], object]] = []\n    for insert, undo in steps:\n        try:\n            insert()\n        except PersistenceError as exc:\n            for undo_done in reversed(completed):\n                undo_done()\n            raise Operational(f\"write failed and was rolled back: {exc}\") from exc\n        completed.append(undo)\n---ACC\n\"\"\"Account rows: the stored account and the live figures the account commands report.\n\n``account_row`` computes the transaction count and the integer-cent balance from the database on\nevery call, so neither figure is stored or embedded.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nAccountRow = tuple[str, str, int, int]\n\n\ndef account_row(db: Database, code: str) -> AccountRow | None:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(account, name, transactions, balance_cents)``, or ``None`` when the account is absent.\"\"\"\n    account = db.accounts.get(account=code)\n    if account is None:\n        return None\n    posted = db.transactions.list(account=code)\n    return (account.account, account.name, len(posted), sum(txn.amount for txn in posted))\n---CFG\n\"\"\"Runtime configuration: where the ledger database lives.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_URL_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef _non_empty(name: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the environment variable's value, or None when unset or empty.\"\"\"\n    value = os.environ.get(name)\n    return value if value else None\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Resolve the database location.\n\n    Precedence: ``DATABASE_URL`` (with an optional leading ``sqlite://`` removed),\n    then ``DATABASE_PATH``, then ``data/app.db``. Unset or empty values are skipped.\n    \"\"\"\n    url = _non_empty(\"DATABASE_URL\")\n    if url is not None:\n        return url.removeprefix(SQLITE_URL_PREFIX)\n    path = _non_empty(\"DATABASE_PATH\")\n    if path is not None:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n---TXNCMD\n\"\"\"Transaction commands: ``ledger txn post|get|delete|amend``.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.registry import Command\nfrom ledger_core.balances import Delete, Edit, Insert, check_no_negative\nfrom ledger_core.errors import NotFound, Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.money import parse_amount\nfrom ledger_core.transactions import next_txn_id, parse_txn_id, txn_row\nfrom ledger_core.validation import validate_date, validate_memo\n\nTXN_HEADER = [\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\"]\nDELETED_HEADER = [\"deleted\"]\n\n\ndef txn_post(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Check every input and the balance rule, then insert one transaction and print its row.\n\n    All checks run before the insert, so a rejected post stores nothing.\n    \"\"\"\n    account, category = args[0], args[1]\n    cents = parse_amount(args[2])\n    day = validate_date(args[3])\n    memo = validate_memo(args[4] if len(args) == 5 else \"\")\n    if db.accounts.get(account=account) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"account {account} does not exist\")\n    if db.categories.get(category=category) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"category {category} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Insert(account=account, amount=cents)])\n    txn = db.transactions.create(\n        txn_id=next_txn_id(db), date=day, account=account, category=category, amount=cents, memo=memo\n    )\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\ndef txn_get(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Print one stored transaction. Read-only; a non-integer id exits 3 and an absent id exits 4.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    txn = db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id)\n    if txn is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\ndef txn_delete(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Remove a transaction unless its account balance would go below zero without it.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    if db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id) is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Delete(txn_id=txn_id)])\n    db.transactions.delete(txn_id=txn_id)\n    return [DELETED_HEADER, [str(txn_id)]]\n\n\ndef txn_amend(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Change only the amount of a transaction, and only when its account stays at or above zero.\"\"\"\n    txn_id = parse_txn_id(args[0])\n    cents = parse_amount(args[1])\n    if db.transactions.get(txn_id=txn_id) is None:\n        raise NotFound(f\"transaction {txn_id} does not exist\")\n    check_no_negative(db, [Edit(txn_id=txn_id, amount=cents)])\n    txn = db.transactions.update(txn_id=txn_id, amount=cents)\n    return [TXN_HEADER, txn_row(txn)]\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"txn\", \"post\"): Command(txn_post, 4, 5),\n    (\"txn\", \"get\"): Command(txn_get, 1, 1),\n    (\"txn\", \"delete\"): Command(txn_delete, 1, 1),\n    (\"txn\", \"amend\"): Command(txn_amend, 2, 2),\n}\n---LEDGER\n#!/bin/sh\n# ledger: command-line cash ledger. Activates .venv when present and hands off to cli.main.\nset -eu\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$ROOT\"\nif [ -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1091\n    set +u; . .venv/bin/activate; set -u\nfi\nexec python -c 'import sys; from cli import main; sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))' \"$@\"\n---BIN\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Run Test Suite\n# Type: batch\n\n# --- Standard Preamble (POSIX sh) ---\nset -eu\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"\nLOG_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/data/logs\"\nmkdir -p \"$LOG_DIR\"\n\nTIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S')\nLOG_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/test_${TIMESTAMP}.log\"\nSTATUS_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/test_${TIMESTAMP}.status\"\n\necho \"=== test started at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ===\" | tee \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Arguments: $*\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Working dir: $PROJECT_DIR\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"---\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\n# Create the environment from the committed lock when it is missing.\nif [ ! -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then\n    uv sync --locked 2>&1 | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nfi\n\n# The pytest exit status is the verdict; tee would hide it, so record it to a file.\n# shellcheck disable=SC1091\n( set +u; . .venv/bin/activate; set -u; pytest -q \"$@\"; echo $? > \"$STATUS_FILE\" ) 2>&1 | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nstatus=$(cat \"$STATUS_FILE\")\nrm -f \"$STATUS_FILE\"\n\necho \"=== test finished at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') with exit $status ===\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nexit \"$status\"\n---PYPROJ\n[project]\nname = \"layerstesting\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = []\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n---CONF\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the ledger test suite.\n\nThe ``db_session`` and ``cli_runner`` fixtures delegate to helpers owned by the\ngenerated ``persistence`` package and the ``cli`` package. Those packages arrive\nwith their own stories, so the imports stay inside the fixtures until then.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Provisioned application store, supplied by ``persistence.testing``.\"\"\"\n    from persistence.testing import db_session as provision\n\n    return provision()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef cli_runner():\n    \"\"\"Command runner that invokes the ``ledger`` CLI, supplied by ``cli.testing``.\"\"\"\n    from cli.testing import cli_runner as provision\n\n    return provision()\n\"\"\"Fixtures shared by the command tests: a fresh, initialised ledger store per test under ``tmp_path``.\n\nCLI writes commit to their own connection, so these tests point ``DATABASE_URL`` at a private file.\nThat keeps ``data/app.db`` out of reach of anything a command does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom persistence import open_database\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef ledger_store(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Point the ledger at an empty, initialised store and return its path.\"\"\"\n    path = tmp_path / \"ledger.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", str(path))\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n    code, _, err = cli_runner(\"init\")\n    assert code == 0, err\n    return path\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef store_open():\n    \"\"\"Open the store at a path for read-back through the persistence interface.\"\"\"\n\n    def opener(path):\n        return open_database(str(path))\n\n    return opener\n---SCHEMA\n-- Generated by Drydock from DATABASE.md. Edit the declaration, not this file.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"accounts\" (\"account\" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, \"name\" TEXT NOT NULL);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"categories\" (\"category\" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, \"description\" TEXT NOT NULL);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions\" (\"txn_id\" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, \"date\" TEXT NOT NULL, \"account\" TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES \"accounts\"(\"account\"), \"category\" TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES \"categories\"(\"category\"), \"amount\" INTEGER NOT NULL, \"memo\" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '');\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_date_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\", \"date\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_category_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"category\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"transactions_account_category_date_idx\" ON \"transactions\" (\"account\", \"category\", \"date\");\n---GIT\n# Runtime\ndata/\n*.db\n*.log\n\n# Environment\n.env\n.venv/\nvenv/\n\n# Python\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n*.egg-info/\ndist/\nbuild/\n.pytest_cache/\n\n# OS\n.DS_Store\nThumbs.db","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01PgHgetWZGEbTXCUQPGfDrx","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GG1mGQHxjRV23rKMF2cPqf","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n---DB\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n---SCHEMAPY\n75:class TransactionsCreateOutput:\n85:class TransactionsGetOutput:\n95:class TransactionsUpdateOutput:\n105:class TransactionsDeleteOutput:\n110:class TransactionsListOutput:\n---TESTLOAD\n\"\"\"``ledger load accounts`` and ``ledger load categories``: all-or-nothing bulk loads with read-back.\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nimport io\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence import PersistenceError\n\nACCOUNT_HEADER = [\"account\", \"name\"]\nCATEGORY_HEADER = [\"category\", \"description\"]\n\n\ndef _write(path, header, rows) -> str:\n    with open(path, \"w\", newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        writer = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n        writer.writerow(header)\n        writer.writerows(rows)\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef _rows(out: str) -> list[list[str]]:\n    return list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n\n\ndef _accounts(store_open, path):\n    with store_open(path) as db:\n        return {row.account: row.name for row in db.accounts.list()}\n\n\ndef _categories(store_open, path):\n    with store_open(path) as db:\n        return {row.category: row.description for row in db.categories.list()}\n\n\n# ── accounts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_accounts_load_reports_count_and_reads_back(ledger_store, store_open, tmp_path):\n    rows = [[\"ZLA1\", \"Load One\"], [\"ZLA2\", \"Load Two\"], [\"ZLA3\", \"Load Three\"]]\n    path = _write(tmp_path / \"accounts.csv\", ACCOUNT_HEADER, rows)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 0, err\n    assert _rows(out) == [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [\"accounts\", \"3\"]]\n    assert _accounts(store_open, ledger_store) == {acct: name for acct, name in rows}\n\n\ndef test_accounts_header_only_loads_zero_rows(ledger_store, tmp_path):\n    path = _write(tmp_path / \"accounts.csv\", ACCOUNT_HEADER, [])\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 0, err\n    assert _rows(out) == [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [\"accounts\", \"0\"]]\n\n\ndef test_accounts_load_accepts_largest_code_and_name(ledger_store, store_open, tmp_path):\n    rows = [[\"Z\" * 12, \"n\" * 40]]\n    path = _write(tmp_path / \"accounts.csv\", ACCOUNT_HEADER, rows)\n    code, _, err = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 0, err\n    assert _accounts(store_open, ledger_store) == {\"Z\" * 12: \"n\" * 40}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"bad\",\n    [\n        [\"zzlc1\", \"Lowercase Code\"],\n        [\"ABCDEFGHIJKLM\", \"Code Too Long\"],\n        [\"ZZ-1\", \"Bad Character\"],\n        [\"\", \"Empty Code\"],\n        [\"ZZL9\", \"\"],\n        [\"ZZL9\", \"x\" * 41],\n        [\"ZZL9\", \"has,comma\"],\n    ],\n)\ndef test_accounts_invalid_row_stores_nothing(ledger_store, store_open, tmp_path, bad):\n    path = _write(tmp_path / \"accounts.csv\", ACCOUNT_HEADER, [[\"ZZLX1\", \"Valid First\"], bad])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert _accounts(store_open, ledger_store) == {}\n\n\ndef ``categories`` are all-or-nothing bulk loads.\n\nEvery row of the file is checked before the first write: the key, the text, the key's repetition\nwithin the file, and the key's presence in the store. The rows are then inserted through\n``ledger_core.atomic.run_all``, so a failing insert removes the rows already stored.\n\n``transactions`` is still a placeholder: it reads and header-checks the file, then exits 1 because\nnothing is loaded, rather than reporting a load that did not happen.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\n\nfrom cli.registry import Command\nfrom ledger_core.atomic import run_all\nfrom ledger_core.csvio import read_rows\nfrom ledger_core.errors import Operational, Rejected\nfrom ledger_core.validation import validate_code, validate_name\n\nACCOUNT_HEADER = (\"account\", \"name\")\nCATEGORY_HEADER = (\"category\", \"description\")\nTRANSACTION_HEADER = (\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\")\n\n\ndef _checked_rows(\n    path: str,\n    header: tuple[str, str],\n    validate_key: Callable[[str], str],\n    stored: Iterable[str],\n) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate every row of ``path`` before any write; return ``(key, text)`` pairs in file order.\"\"\"\n    already_stored = set(stored)\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    checked: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    for line, (key_text, text) in read_rows(path, header):\n        try:\n            key = validate_key(key_text)\n            validate_name(text)\n        except Rejected as exc:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: {exc}\") from exc\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} repeats within the file\")\n        if key in already_stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: code {key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n        checked.append((key, text))\n    return checked\n\n\ndef _load(\n    path: str,\n    header: tuple[str, str],\n    table: str,\n    validate_key: Callable[[str], str],\n    stored: Iterable[str],\n    create: Callable[[str, str], object],\n    remove: Callable[[str], object],\n) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Check the whole file, insert every row as one unit, and report the loaded count.\"\"\"\n    checked = _checked_rows(path, header, validate_key, stored)\n    run_all([(_insert(create, key, text), _remove(remove, key)) for key, text in checked])\n    return [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [table, str(len(checked))]]\n\n\ndef _insert(create: Callable[[str, str], object], key: str, text: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: create(key, text)\n\n\ndef _remove(remove: Callable[[str], object], key: str) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    return lambda: remove(key)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``account,name`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        ACCOUNT_HEADER,\n        \"accounts\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.account for row in db.accounts.list()),\n        lambda key, name: db.accounts.create(account=key, name=name),\n        lambda key: db.accounts.delete(account=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef load_categories(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``category,description`` rows from ``args[0]``; nothing is stored unless every row is valid.\"\"\"\n    return _load(\n        args[0],\n        CATEGORY_HEADER,\n        \"categories\",\n        validate_code,\n        (row.category for row in db.categories.list()),\n        lambda key, text: db.categories.create(category=key, description=text),\n        lambda key: db.categories.delete(category=key),\n    )\n\n\ndef _transactions_placeholder(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    read_rows(args[0], TRANSACTION_HEADER)\n    raise Operational(\"loading transactions is not implemented yet\")\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"load\", \"accounts\"): Command(load_accounts, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"categories\"): Command(load_categories, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"transactions\"): Command(_transactions_placeholder, 1, 1),\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":17,"newStart":4,"newLines":20,"lines":[" within the file, and the key's presence in the store. ``(txn_id, date, account, category, cents, memo)``.\"\"\"\n    stored_ids = {txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()}\n    accounts = {row.account for row in db.accounts.list()}\n    categories = {row.category for row in db.categories.list()}\n    seen: set[int] = set()\n    checked: list[TxnRow] = []\n    for line, (id_text, day, account, category, amount_text, memo) in read_rows(path, TRANSACTION_HEADER):\n        try:\n            txn_id = parse_txn_id(id_text)\n            validate_date(day)\n            cents = parse_amount(amount_text)\n            validate_memo(memo)\n        except Rejected as exc:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: {exc}\") from exc\n        if account not in accounts:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: account {account} does not exist\")\n        if category not in categories:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: category {category} does not exist\")\n        if txn_id in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: transaction {txn_id} repeats within the file\")\n        if txn_id in stored_ids:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{path} line {line}: transaction {txn_id} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(txn_id)\n        checked.append((txn_id, day, account, category, cents, memo))\n    return checked\n\n\ndef _insert_txn(db, row: TxnRow) -> Callable[[], object]:\n    txn_id, day, account, category, cents, memo = row\n    return lambda: db.transactions.create(\n        txn_id=txn_id, date=day, account=account, category=category, amount=cents, memo=memo\n    )\n\n\ndef load_transactions(db, args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Load ``txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo`` rows from ``args[0]``; all or nothing.\n\n    The balance rule is judged over the whole file's net effect per account, so a withdrawal listed\n    before its funding deposit is accepted when the final balance is not below zero.\n    \"\"\"\n    checked = _checked_transactions(db, args[0])\n    check_no_negative(db, [Insert(account=account, amount=cents) for _, _, account, _, cents, _ in checked])\n    run_all([(_insert_txn(db, row), _remove(db.transactions.delete, row[0])) for row in checked])\n    return [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [\"transactions\", str(len(checked))]]\n\n\nCOMMANDS = {\n    (\"load\", \"accounts\"): Command(load_accounts, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"categories\"): Command(load_categories, 1, 1),\n    (\"load\", \"transactions\"): Command(load_transactions, 1,
